name_note: Most genomes GTDB places in this species carry the NCBI name Adlercreutzia equolifaciens, a closely related named species, so papers may use either name.

sentences.text: Adlercreutzia rubneri was proposed as a novel species for strain ResAG-91, an anaerobic, Gram-positive, rod-shaped bacterium isolated from a faecal sample of a male human volunteer.
Strain ResAG-91 was able to metabolize the stilbene resveratrol into dihydroresveratrol, and its genome size is 2.8 Mbp with a G+C content of 63.3 mol%.

The closely related species Adlercreutzia equolifaciens was reported, in shotgun metagenomic analyses, to be depleted in patients with liver diseases such as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease compared with healthy controls.
The same study reported that Adlercreutzia equolifaciens possesses anti-inflammatory properties in vitro and in vivo in a humanized mouse model.
